content: The lift plan is a comprehensive document that serves as the blueprint for the entire lifting operation, detailing how it will be carried out safely. A detailed lift plan must include several key components. It begins with a thorough risk assessment, identifying all potential hazards associated with the lift and outlining specific control measures to mitigate them. This includes assessing ground conditions to ensure the ground can support the crane and its load, calculating the required size of outrigger mats to distribute the pressure, and checking for overhead obstructions like power lines or nearby structures. The plan must specify the crane to be used, including its configuration (boom length, counterweight, etc.) and provide calculations to confirm it has adequate capacity for the planned lift radius and load weight. A critical part of the plan is the rigging study, which details the specific slings, shackles, and other gear to be used, their capacities, and the method of attachment to the load. The lift plan also includes a step-by-step sequence of the lifting operation, from crane setup to load placement and crane demobilization. It must clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each member of the lift team, including the lift supervisor, crane operator, rigger, and signal person.
